prompts.text: Name a part of the human body you can see from the outside
Name an animal that is native to Australia
Name a person who has won an Olympic gold medal (Summer or Winter Games)
Name a component found inside a desktop computer or laptop
Name a piece of equipment you'd find in a school or science laboratory
Name an amphibian (any frog, toad, newt, salamander or caecilian)
Name a man who scored in a men's FIFA World Cup final (own goals and shootout penalties don't count)
Name a software framework or library (any programming language)
Name a substance that is a gas at room temperature (mixtures like air count)
Name a mushroom or any other kind of fungus
Name a word or phrase used in cricket
Name a computing acronym or abbreviation (like USB)
Name a scientific law, principle or effect named after a person (like Boyle's law)
Name a cactus or any other succulent plant
Name a word or phrase used in American football
Name a person who founded or co-founded a well-known tech company
Name a type of cell found in the human body
Name an animal that lives in the Arctic or the Antarctic
Name a word or phrase used in baseball
Name a camera brand or camera maker, past or present
Name a metal alloy (like bronze)
Name a rodent (rabbits and hares don't count)
Name an NBA team, current or former (BAA teams count; the nickname alone is fine)
Name a famous computer model or system from history (any era, any size)
Name a kind of object or phenomenon found in outer space (a type, not one specific named object)
Name an animal that has hooves
Name a famous sports stadium or arena (current or demolished)
Name a company that designs or makes computer chips or processors
Name a part of the human brain
Name a body part that some animals have but humans don't (like a beak)
